name: The Brill road (water-meadow causeway, clay hill and toll-bar)
region: Lordaeron, north from the river depot's town toward Brill

sensoryProfile.sight: A lord's causeway of stone and packed gravel across water-meadows, flat; then up off the meadows between hedges onto yellow clay with old deep ruts slumped at the shoulders; a toll-bar over the next rise: pole across the road, stone hut, a garden with fine beans. Dark water-meadows smoking pale on both sides at night.
sensoryProfile.sound: Hooves ringing on the stone causeway.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: A road that holds nothing: the wild goose chase the overseer sent them on.

establishedFacts.fact: The toll-keeper (thin, brown, leather apron, a day-book) says no grain has come this way in over a month (four wagons from the river depot for the Brill mills, the last), only a tinker, a lord's steward and boy, sheep for market, and a company of King's foot a week ago cutting across to the hill road for the prince, who do not pay. 'Grain pays.'

Rain fell before dawn on the morning they left the sick village; ruts that stood in it are slumped; six loaded wagons after that rain would have cut sharp edges. Only single ridden horses, a one-wheeled barrow, sheep, and one narrow, empty light cart. Cyndia: nothing heavy since the rain.
The overseer's 'fork past the chapel' and 'stone at the fork' lead onto this road.
The mare of Jaina's went down on its knees on the causeway on the return in the dark and came up with the mage still on it.
They watered at a ford at noon on the way out.

eventsHere.event: A day's ride north on the overseer's lie; Sylvanas realises there were never any wagons; the party turns back at sunset.
